newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BOLOGNA STAND UP POPE BUT STILL DRAW.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BOLOGNA STAND UP POPE BUT STILL DRAW.

text.p: Pope John Paul rather than team tactics figured large in post-match analysis by Italian serie A side Bologna following their 1-1 draw with Roma on Sunday.
Bologna provoked a minor diplomatic incident on Saturday when they failed to show up for a private audience at the Vatican with the Pope.
At the Olympic Stadium in Rome on Sunday, embarrassed club president Giuseppe Gazzoni Frascara was at pains to apologise for the gaffe rather than comment on his side's match performance.
"We apologise to the Pontiff for not making the visit...But it's not true to suggest that we preferred to go training rather than visit the Pope," Frascara said.

"The truth is that it's difficult to travel in Italy...The team got delayed 45 minutes on a routine scheduled flight (from Bologna to Rome)...and at that stage it simply wasn't possible to guarantee that we would arrive at the Vatican in time."
Even if the incident provoked dismay in the Vatican, it seems that the sporting gods were in a forgiving mood.
Bologna picked up a useful away point in a game vital to the UEFA Cup qualifying prospects of both teams.
